title:
When Local Closure Becomes Globally Wrong
By Dr. Moh Kolbehdari
gist: Dr. Moh Kolbehdari argues that in advanced heterogeneous packaging several individually accurate domain analyses (die, package, PCB, thermal, electromigration) can still describe an inconsistent system because their boundary conditions are coupled; the next challenge is physical continuity across simulation boundaries, not just per-domain fidelity.

themes.theme: Local accuracy is not system correctness

insights.claim: In a high-current heterogeneous package, individually accurate die-extraction, package, PCB PDN, thermal and electromigration analyses can still describe an inconsistent physical system because their boundary conditions are connected.
insights.speaker: Dr. Moh Kolbehdari
insights.so_what: Multiphysics coupling, not single-tool accuracy, is the real sign-off challenge for advanced packaging.
insights.quote: Individually, none of those analyses has to be wrong.

insights.claim: A local temperature rise changes conductor resistivity, which shifts current distribution, power dissipation and electromigration stress, which in turn alters the temperature distribution, so thermal and electrical behavior are coupled across separate tools.
insights.speaker: Dr. Moh Kolbehdari
insights.so_what: Requires coupled electro-thermal simulation rather than sequential single-domain runs.

insights.claim: Return current follows physical geometry rather than organizational ownership, so a board-level stackup or reference-plane change can invalidate package-analysis assumptions that were perfectly reasonable when originally completed.
insights.speaker: Dr. Moh Kolbehdari
insights.so_what: Sign-off must span package and board together, not be handed across organizational silos.

themes.theme: From accurate domains to a consistent whole path

insights.claim: The emerging challenge in heterogeneous integration is physical continuity across simulation boundaries, moving from accurate models of individual domains toward physically consistent models of the complete path.
insights.speaker: Dr. Moh Kolbehdari
insights.so_what: Opportunity for cross-domain co-simulation and continuity-checking EDA tools.
insights.quote: It is physical continuity across simulation boundaries.

insights.claim: As systems move toward chiplets, HBM, advanced substrates and higher current density, domain coupling strengthens and local sign-off becomes progressively less equivalent to system sign-off.
insights.speaker: Dr. Moh Kolbehdari
insights.so_what: AI/HPC packaging trends make isolated verification increasingly unreliable.
